tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__edit_version
tools.description: Publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit (some clients refuse any artifact but your own as owner-only), by replacing text in its current document: use it for a small change instead of sending the whole page to publish_version. The server reads the live index.html, applies every edit in order, and publishes the result as one new version; if any edit cannot be applied, nothing is published. Each old_text must occur exactly once in the document as it stands when that edit is applied: include enough surrounding text to make it unique. base_version must name the live version (from get_artifact, read_artifact, list_files or your last publish result); if it is no longer live the call is rejected with a conflict that names the live version: read what you are changing again and retry. To rename the artifact pass title, which also rewrites the document's <title> element; an edit to that element without title is refused, because the server keeps it in step with the artifact's title. Artifacts that contain a live (collaboratively edited) document cannot be edited here. An artifact made from a type is edited only if this server offers list_files, and only with path: one of its own text files, as list_files lists them, never its page or its type's files.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_files
tools.description: Publish an artifact from files on disk: their bytes go from the files to the artifact and do not pass through you. Prefer this to publish_version when the page's files already exist, when there is more than one file or an image, or when the page is large. For each file give `as`, the path it is served at, and `path`, its absolute path on the machine where your own file tools run; leave `uri` out. index.html is required in a new artifact. Limits for one call: 256 files, 20 MiB a file, 64 MiB in all. The client may refuse a file it will not send, such as a secrets file, a link or a path outside the working folder. Omit slug to create an artifact, private to you. To republish, give slug and base_version (from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish); title and icon are kept when omitted. A republish changes only the files named and keeps the rest, which stay served: to take a file away, list it in remove. mode "replace" makes the files named the whole artifact and drops the rest. This tool publishes only to an artifact of yours. **Files Claude did not write**: Claude reads the whole file before publishing it, even when the person asks it not to. Publishing distributes the content, and Claude never distributes what it has not seen. A request for privacy is a reason to read before publishing, not an exemption. If Claude cannot read the file, it does not publish it. **Claude never publishes** a page that impersonates a real person or organization, for example by using their name, branding, byline or domain. Claude also never publishes fabricated records, receipts or reviews presented as genuine, forms or flows that collect credentials or payment details under false pretenses, or content that targets a private individual. Claude refuses whether it wrote the page or the person supplied it, and whatever purpose is claimed, such as a prop or a test, when the page would work as the real thing. If publishing is refused, Claude does not suggest other ways to host or share the page.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_version
tools.description: Publish an artifact: either create a new artifact — omit slug and give title and content; you become its owner and it starts private to you — or publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit — give slug and base_version. Some clients may publish only to your own artifacts: there the call is refused as owner-only. Republishing is read-then-send: base_version must name the live version you are replacing (from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish result) — if it is no longer live, the publish is rejected with a conflict; re-read and retry from the current state. On success the new version goes live immediately. When republishing, the artifact's stored connectors manifest carries forward unchanged, and so do title, favicon, icon and contract when omitted. Content is capped at 16 MiB.

schema.description: Publish an artifact: either create a new artifact — omit slug and give title and content; you become its owner and it starts private to you — or publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit — give slug and base_version. Some clients may publish only to your own artifacts: there the call is refused as owner-only. Rejected with a conflict if it no longer names the live version, so concurrent edits are never silently overwritten. Omit when creating.

contract.description: Optional runtime-contract version (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH). Leave it out to keep the current one. Pass one only when the user asks for a different version, or this server's answer says to. If the publish is rejected because the contract is yanked or out of the supported window, republish with an explicit "0.0.0" to clear the contract — omitting the argument is not a reliable recovery (the server may carry the stored contract forward, repeating the rejection).

Omit it for ordinary edits (open pages then move at their next quiet moment); it cannot be relaxed once published.

favicon.description: Optional legacy emoji marker; omit it.

icon.description: One short, generic word for the artifact's tab icon — a plain signifier of what it is, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map; not a product or brand name. Pass one when creating; omit when republishing to keep the current icon.

shared_live.description: States who the artifact you are republishing is already shared with, and changes nothing: its 'read' value from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish result. Required when that value is 'users' (named people or groups), 'org' (the user's whole organization) or 'public' (anyone with the link). Leave it out for a new artifact and when the value is 'owner'. Rejected if it does not match the artifact's current value.

slug.description: The artifact's server-assigned slug (UUID), e.g. from list_artifacts, get_artifact or the artifact's own URL. Omit to create a new artifact.

title.description: Browser-tab title. Required when creating. When republishing it is optional — omitted, the new version keeps the current live version's title (the server also keeps the stored HTML's <title> element in sync with it); pass a value only to rename the artifact, never invent a new title on a routine republish.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__read_artifact
tools.description: Read the current document of an artifact: one that the user owns, or one that belongs to someone in the user's organization and that the user can open. Read a pasted claude.ai artifact link with this tool. Returns a JSON summary (slug, version id, title, favicon, runtime-contract version, total_lines, and for a multi-file artifact its file names), then the HTML of the version the user is served, then a reminder. The HTML, and the summary's title, favicon and file names, are wrapped in an <untrusted-document-...> tag that the summary's notice names; the tag is not part of them. A document over ~1 MiB is not served whole: read it in parts with offset and limit, which count lines; next_offset says where the next part starts. A part is a piece of the document: never send one to publish_version as the whole page. Artifacts that contain a live (collaboratively edited) document are not served. For a multi-file artifact only the entry document (index.html) is returned. Use this tool before republishing an artifact: change the page with edit_version, or send the whole edited HTML to publish_version, with base_version set to the returned version. Use read_shared_artifact instead for an artifact in the user's organization that the user does not own and that an agent or a Coworker owns, can write to or has written to, or that someone outside that organization has written to. After read_artifact answers not found, do not try read_shared_artifact: it answers the same. read_artifact serves the live version of an artifact the user can edit, otherwise the version shared with the user.

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- At task completion, close tabs created for the task that are no longer needed.
  Keep a tab open if the user needs to see it, it is needed for a known follow-up,
  or closing it could discard unsaved work or other important state.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background. Never call `activate_tab(target)` automatically: it brings Chrome
  to the foreground. Call it only when the user explicitly asks to see or
  visibly switch to that tab. Do not pair `switch_tab()` with `activate_tab()`.

  task, card, or agent. Omit `BU_NAME` and reuse the default daemon for normal
  sequential local work across websites, tabs, screenshots, and Codex turns.
  Do not invent per-job names such as `gmail1375` or `slack1371`: every new
  local daemon opens another browser-level CDP connection and Chrome may show
  another Allow prompt.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.

  Chrome. Keep using background CDP operations. For a focus-gated page,
  temporarily call `cdp("Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled", enabled=True)`,
  perform and verify the operation, then disable it in a `finally` block. If

  activating the tab. Do not invent a `Runtime.evaluate` scroll replacement or

Desktop Commander provides tools for working with the user's authorized device.

# Re-review rulings — 2026-10-27 (delegated: the user said "just use best judgment")

Marker for every edit that applies one of these: *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling Rn)*.
In-text record where a decision is stated: "Resolved 2026-10-27 — delegated ruling Rn (re-review; user delegated to best judgment): ..."
These rulings never reverse a prior user ruling; they settle consequences the user's rulings left ambiguous or unimplementable.

## General rules (G)
- G1 Owner wins: where two GDDs disagree on a value, field, unit or contract, the registry `source:` GDD wins and the other conforms. If the thing is unregistered, the PUBLISHER of the field/signal/value wins and the consumer conforms.
- G2 Specialist disagreements: follow the creative-director's stated resolution in that GDD's disagreements list. Where the CD said "the user should choose", take the CD's stated lean.
- G3 Carried-over blockers (flagged "still not fixed"/"carried over"): previous edits did not land. After each edit, Grep for the old wording and confirm it is gone everywhere in the GDD (body, examples, ACs, tuning tables, OQs).
- G4 ACs that contradict the GDD's own formulas: recompute from the formula at registry defaults; never weaken a formula to match an AC.
- G5 Division/overflow at boundaries: guard explicitly (e.g. avail == 0 -> share 0, everything unserved); state the guard in the formula and add a boundary AC.

## Cross-cutting rulings (R)
- R1 Restore epoch (consequence of X8/D16). Save/Load OWNS `restore_epoch` as a persisted integer in the save slot header (u32, starts 0). On every restore (death restart or load), Save/Load increments it and durably writes the header (atomic header-only write) BEFORE the first RUNNING tick, so reloading the same autosave twice, in-process or after a fresh process start, gives a new epoch each time. The kernel exposes it read-only in `kernel.clock` as (T, world_seed, restore_epoch) — sim-visible, pure. The KERNEL (command-simulation-layer.md) owns the one derivation for threat draws, counter_eff = rng_counter + RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE x restore_epoch, and owns RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE (value 1048576 unchanged; registry_request: move its source from attention-system.md to command-simulation-layer.md, with attention, horror and save-load in referenced_by). The stream name hash stays cached and unchanged. Attention and Horror call the kernel derivation; neither defines its own. Graph physical failures and persisted counters never read the epoch. Determinism (G3/G4) is defined given (save bytes, restore_epoch): the same pair replays identically; tests pin the epoch. Required ACs: (i) two successive restores of the same save yield epochs e and e+1 and different threat draws; (ii) a fresh-process reload of the same slot also advances the epoch; (iii) same (save, epoch) pair -> identical draws. Save/Load's 'none of it able to alter the sim' is amended to exempt restore_epoch.
- R2 seq (kernel CR-4). The kernel stamps `seq` internally per (peer, source); callers never choose it; `submit()` stays void (fire-and-forget). A caller may attach an opaque `correlation` field (int) that the kernel echoes unchanged in the result/rejection event. Player Controller keys pre-play tokens by `correlation`. # Second delegated rulings — 2026-10-28 (the user: "use your own best judgement, fix the remaining issues, name whatever you need yourself")

Marker for every edit: *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling Rn)* or *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*.
In-text record: "Resolved 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling Rn (user delegated all remaining calls, including naming the reference machine): ...".
G1-G5 and R1-R10 of rr-rulings.md stay binding except where amended below. R11 (X14 stays open) is SUPERSEDED by R12.

## G6 Cross-GDD edits are now allowed
A blocker that needs a sibling GDD to change is fixed IN the sibling. Owner wins (G1): the registry `source:` GDD, else the publisher of the field/signal, keeps its value; the other conforms. Each file has exactly one writer per pass; requests to another file go to that file's writer.
Classify every blocker first: **CONFLICT** (the same thing has two values/contracts in two GDDs) -> the owner's value stands and the other GDD conforms; **GAP** (the owner lacks a surface, exemption, field or signal that a consumer's user-ruled or delegated-ruled behaviour requires, e.g. Interaction's act_gate exempt list lacking self-patch, HUD lacking a give_up surface) -> the OWNER ADDS it, and the consumer's requirement is the spec. Never "fix" a gap by removing the consumer's ruled behaviour.
Precedence: where R1 text conflicts with R13/R14, R13/R14 win; re-mark such text "delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13/R14".

## R12 Reference machines and build (closes X14; supersedes R11)
- **RM-DESKTOP (minimum-spec desktop):** Windows 10/11 64-bit; 6-core/6-thread CPU of the Intel Core i5-9400F / AMD Ryzen 5 2600 class; 8 GB RAM; GPU of the NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 Ti 4 GB / AMD Radeon RX 570 4 GB class (Vulkan 1.2+); SATA SSD; 1920x1080 at 60 Hz. P99 CPU frame-time ceiling 16.6 ms.
- **RM-DECK (handheld):** Steam Deck LCD (2022), SteamOS stable, 1280x800 at 60 Hz panel, 30 fps target. P99 CPU frame-time ceiling 33.3 ms.
- **Build type for every wall-clock figure:** a release export (Godot 4.7.2 release export template, not the editor and not a debug template), renderer `forward_plus` (project.godot), vsync on, the pipeline's warm-up of 120 frames, with the startup read-back (renderer, driver) recorded with each result.
- **P99 headroom:** pass needs P99 <= 90 % of the ceiling (headroom >= 1.7 ms desktop, >= 3.3 ms Deck).
- The developer's machine is not a reference machine; figures from it are indicative only.
- Recorded in `project.yaml` as `qa.min_spec` (done by the orchestrator). In GDDs: replace "X14 open / not named / [blocked: reference hardware]" with the named machines; performance ACs become gated on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK at the spike (still measured at the spike, so a value not yet measured is "pending spike", not "blocked").

## R13 OQ-50: Continue of a Save & Quit keeps the epoch (amends R1)
User ruling D16 ("not steerable by quit") outranks delegated R1. A **death-stub restore** advances `restore_epoch` (durably, R14). A **Continue** that restores a `QUIT` generation which is the newest non-demoted verified generation **carries the epoch unchanged** (no epoch write). A Continue of any other generation (after a kill, crash or fallback) advances it. ACs: (i) death restore -> e+1 and different threat draws; (ii) Save & Quit, Continue -> same epoch, identical draws; (iii) kill, Continue of an AUTO/EVENT generation -> e+1; (iv) same (save, epoch) -> identical draws.

## R14 Where the epoch lives and when it is durable (fixes kernel CR-15 vs SL-23 and the REBASED-key/trailer-SHA defect)
- `restore_epoch` is stored in a **per-slot side file** `slot_epoch.bin` (u32 + CRC32), written atomically (temp file + rename) by the Save/Load worker. It is **not** in any generation file, so generation bytes and every trailer SHA and every key derived from them never change.
- When an advance is due (R13), Save/Load issues the epoch write in a **pre-restore staging step, before calling `request_restore`**, polls it per frame (never blocks the main thread), and calls `request_restore(gen, restore_epoch)` only after `EPOCH_DURABLE`. The kernel's LOADING stays atomic within one boundary service. Kernel CR-15 is reworded to: "Save/Load's epoch staging step has completed (EPOCH_DURABLE, or a logged SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE with save_status = FAILED)", and the kernel lists the failure-path exposure too.
- If the write fails or exceeds `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` (500 ms placeholder), the restore proceeds with the advanced epoch in memory, logs `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` and sets `save_status = FAILED` (the device is failing; saving is impossible anyway). This is a **listed exposure**: a kill before any later successful write may replay that epoch once. The ACs for durability are scoped to the success path; the failure path has its own AC (logged, status FAILED, play continues).
- A missing or corrupt `slot_epoch.bin` reads as `max(epoch recorded in the newest generation's header copy, 0) + 1`. Each generation header also records the epoch at write time (read-only copy, for recovery).

## R15 OQ-52: confirmed option (a)
A `QUIT` generation without `VITALS` in its `risky_cause` is exempt from the fairness step-back. Confirmed; drop "USER DECISION".

## R16 OQ-DO-30: option (A)
The playtest preset registers only `debug_overlay_mark`; `debug_overlay_reveal` is dev-only. A tester session can never leave `HIDDEN`. Update DO-2/6/8, AC-DO-170, AC-DO-185.

## R17 Interaction OQ 48: confirmed
A wounded victim is not guaranteed an escape (Pillar 3, honest horror). Confirmed; no cooldown or damage floor.

## R18 Player Controller OQ 29(ii): pre-ruled conditional
If the target-acquisition spike fails and the lighter fallbacks do not close the gap, `aim_indicator` defaults ON for mouse players (still player-toggleable). Until then D9 (off by default) stands.

## R19 Boarding OQ-BS-34 fallback: pre-ruled conditional
If the boarding spike finds no K3 pass line inside 21-28 tiles with Attention's levers, the X3 route band's upper end widens to 31 tiles for the reference sortie (lower end stays 21). Not applied now; the spike decides.

## R20 Every "default applied, pending user confirmation" is confirmed
Every item marked "Default applied ... pending user confirmation" or "(confirm)" in any GDD is confirmed as of 2026-10-28 by delegation. Re-mark it "confirmed 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R20" and remove it from open user-decision lists. Do not change the value.

## R21 Remaining "USER DECISION" items
Any other "USER DECISION" left in a GDD is decided by its creative-director lean (G2) or, absent one, by the option that preserves prior user rulings and needs the least new content; record it as delegated ruling R21 with one sentence of reason. Never leave a "USER DECISION" open.

content.content:
**PC-6. One focus model, interaction reach, lit-only actions, hold-to-confirm.** *Reach* is a sector from the foot origin: `REACH_PX` = 72 base px (1.5 tiles — the adjacent ring including diagonals at 68 px), half-angle `REACH_HALF_ANGLE_DEG` = 70° about the **facing**. Objects behind the player are never candidates. *Focus — the same model on every device:* among interactables that are in reach, in the arc and **lit** (Emitter State's exposure query above the technical-artist's threshold), the focused one minimises `score = d / REACH_PX + FOCUS_AIM_WEIGHT × θ / REACH_HALF_ANGLE_DEG`, with `θ` the angle between the object's direction from the foot origin and the **ground-projected aim** (mouse: the direction from the foot origin to `cursor_aim_world`, PC-5; stick and keys: the committed aim, a direction only) and `FOCUS_AIM_WEIGHT` = 1.0 (0.5–2.0), `FOCUS_STICKY_MARGIN` = 0.10 (D.9) — **aim-weighted proximity** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: measuring θ from the chest-height aim origin made a floor object the player points straight at read 30° off; the focus score is Adapter-side presentation, so the ground projection changes no sim value, and `in_reach` is untouched)*; the mouse has no separate pick-under-cursor path (the cursor moves the aim, and aim weights the score, so the model is one). Exactly one object is focused; the HUD draws its prompt (`E · Cut`) only when lit (art bible 7.0), at `world_to_hud(target)`; an off-screen object has no prompt (C9). **The Adapter never chooses the verb**: `interact` is one button, and **Interaction declares, per focused object and equipped tool, the command type and its mode** ∈ {`TAP`, `HOLD_CONFIRM`, `CHANNEL`}; the Adapter applies the matching policy over the same commands. **Decision (art bible 7.0 leaves it to the game-designer): an action is possible only on a lit object.** Interaction's `validate` calls the exposure query the prompt uses, so the prompt never lies by omission. *Rationale:* "what you light, you can read" must also be "what you light, you can touch", or working in the dark becomes a free Attention dodge and "go dark" degenerates into the dominant strategy; light has to cost Attention for darkness to be a trade. Exceptions are Interaction's `act_gate` exempt rows (registry `act_gate`): `drop` of the carried module, `toggle_beam`, the inspect card of an already-lit instrument, `throw_glowstick` and, by the resolution below, every `ACTOR_SELF` verb. **Resolved 2026-10-27 — delegated ruling G1 with the re-review's recommendation (re-review; user delegated to best judgment): option (a), `ACTOR_SELF` verbs are an `act_gate` exempt row (Open Question 16).** The self-patch (`begin_patch` on object class `ACTOR_SELF`, Interaction IA-17) is the only MVP way to repair the suit (Suit SE-22). As Interaction, Emitter State and the registry stood it could never pass the lit check: Emitter State EM-21 adds the owner's own beam to the owner's `lux_pm` only and states it "is not added to the owner's `act_lux_pm`" (the player is never the target of their own verb), the `lit` flag is computed from `act_lux_pm`, and Interaction listed `NOT_LIT` for `begin_patch`, so a player alone with the lamp on got `NOT_LIT`. "What you light, you can touch" was never meant to read "you cannot patch your own suit in the dark"; read that way the Pillar 3 "go dark" lever would be a trap. So `ACTOR_SELF` verbs join the exempt rows beside `drop`, `toggle_beam`, the inspect card and `throw_glowstick`; EM-21's "never the target of your own verb" stays intact everywhere else. The "known defect" wording is withdrawn. Consequences stated here so the siblings can conform: the lamp-off result is `Applied` (patching yourself in the dark is legal), and the mid-channel unlit re-check of PC-7 (v) skips a channel whose target class is `ACTOR_SELF`, because there is no lit object to lose. **The siblings are not edited here and must conform before the vertical-slice story set:** the registry `act_gate` exempt list (owner Interaction), Interaction IA-6 and Emitter State's EM-21 note; until they do, the acceptance criterion in Acceptance Criteria is a conformance test that fails against them. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; re-review, delegated ruling G1)* Web Map & Transit's request to exempt `pod_hop` from the lit conjunct (ASK-I2) is Interaction's to accept in `act_gate`; `in_reach` (D.9) keeps its lit conjunct. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from web-map-and-transit)* *Hold-to-confirm* (`HOLD_CONFIRM` mode — destructive verbs, HR-14): a **local** hold of `CONFIRM_HOLD_S` = 0.8 s (0.6–1.2) in render time, drawn on the art bible 7.3 **linear bar — never a ring** (routed correction to the kernel's "progress ring" wording); **release drains the bar at 2×**; on completion one command is submitted; the sim never sees a partial hold. Option: **tap-to-confirm** — two taps, arm then confirm, within `CONFIRM_TAP_WINDOW` = 3 s. No QTEs anywhere. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; D.10 has the arithmetic.)* **Hardening:** (i) each frame adds at most `CONFIRM_DT_MAX_S` = 0.05 s to the bar, so a single 1 s hitch cannot confirm a destructive cut; (ii) the target is **latched** while the bar is above zero: a focus change during a hold neither transfers nor completes the bar, it drains at 2× on the latched target and the new focus starts from zero after release; (iii) modes are exclusive per declaration (IA-8): a `HOLD_CONFIRM` verb submits one `TAP`-class command on completion and never a `begin_*`; if a future verb needs confirm-then-work, Interaction declares it as a `CHANNEL` with a confirm step, the completed bar submits `begin_<verb>`, the plate resets to zero and the HUD re-fills it from the channel's committed progress, and the held `interact` then sustains the channel in hold mode (the "release before re-arm" rule belongs to the confirm bar only); (iv) the tap-window timer is frozen while the kernel is `PAUSED` and disarms on context change.
---
**PC-7. Channels (cut / weld / patch).** `interact` on an object whose declared mode is `CHANNEL` → the Adapter submits `begin_<verb> {target}` (`coalesce = NONE`; owner Interaction, Assembly behind it for weld/cut). The owner's `validate` requires: lit and in reach, **`controller.state.intent_octant == NONE`**, not carrying, not staggered/downed. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: `intent_octant` and `intent_run` are written by the `set_move_intent` `apply` handler in P2; `octant` is the value `controller.step` publishes in P3 and the channel owners' hooks read. Validation that read `octant` saw last tick's value, so releasing W and pressing E in one frame was rejected, and pressing W and E together was accepted and then aborted silently. With the split the first applies and the second is rejected at once with reason `MOVING` (immediate class, "no" cue; proposed to Interaction, today folded into `BUSY` — Open Question 25). Both rely on the Adapter submitting intents before commands in a frame (PC-2).)* **Progress is sim state in `interaction.state`** (with `owner_system` ASSEMBLY for weld and section cut), accrued per tick by Interaction's hook; the owner's `apply` records `channel_ref` and `channel_face` through the Controller's `set_channel_ref(actor, owner_system, channel_id, face_octant)` mutator (PC-1 b) and the Controller holds facing at `channel_face` (PC-4 rule 2); `loco_state` becomes `CHANNELLING` in that tick's `controller.step` by the precedence function of States and Transitions *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from modular-ship-assembly, interaction-system)* **Hold is the default; a toggle option exists; both are Adapter policy over the same two commands.** *Interrupts:* (i) **release** (hold mode) or a second press / `cancel` (toggle mode) → `cancel_channel`; (ii) **movement** — `controller.step` itself clears `channel_ref` and `channel_face` in the tick an applied intent has `octant ≠ NONE` (step 3 of the `controller.step` order, so the move wins on that same tick and the first movement step is not lost), and the owner's hook, declared `after: controller.step`, reads `controller.state.octant` and aborts (sim-side, so identical in `MIRROR`; the 8-way dead-zone already filters stick drift) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; (iii) **stagger / downed** — the Controller Sim clears `channel_ref`; (iv) **target invalidated** (power drops mid-cut, the section detaches) — the owner aborts and reports through state change, never through the command result (CR-5); (v) **unlit** — the owner re-checks the target's `lit` every `LIT_RECHECK_TICKS` (6, Interaction IA-7) and aborts `UNLIT` (not for a channel whose target class is `ACTOR_SELF`: that verb is `act_gate`-exempt, PC-6, Open Question 16 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*); **proposed grace** (accessibility; Interaction's to adopt, Open Question 25): `LIT_ABORT_GRACE_TICKS` = 30 (0–60, extendable by an accessibility setting) is a counter to which each consecutive dark check adds `LIT_RECHECK_TICKS` (so 30 = five consecutive dark checks) and a lit check resets, so tremor, stick drift or sliding off a narrow beam edge no longer aborts a 360-tick weld while a lamp that is switched off still aborts within half a second *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; (vi) a body transfer, a restore, and entry to `chart_table` or `chat` (Contexts, PC-2). The player keeps control of the body at all times: a channel never locks movement, movement cancels the channel. *Rationale:* Dread Before Chaos needs "I can leave now" to be true in every state. **Pause:** the tick stops, progress freezes; on resume the hold survives if the button is still down (PC-2 resync). Whether partial progress persists on the target after an abort is **Interaction's rule** (IA-16). Channel feedback (sounds → audio-director): *start* (pre-play: hand animation + tool start sound + bar appears), *confirmed* (bar begins filling from committed state), *progress* (work loop + tool loop sound), *cancel* (release: bar drains at 2×, tool stops), *abort* (owner-driven: bar snaps empty, a distinct interrupted cue), *completion* (bar fills, completion cue, work loop ends), *rejection* (immediate class: ack withdrawn within a frame, a dull "no" cue); a free-lie-detector channel is never a rejection — it is identical to *confirmed* until it resolves to its `PRECONDITION` outcome (KRN:96). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from interaction-system)* "Stopped", "interrupted" and "nothing happened" are three different sounds.
---
- **If the player self-patches** (`begin_patch` on `ACTOR_SELF`): see PC-6 and Open Question 16 — resolved by option (a): `ACTOR_SELF` verbs are an `act_gate` exempt row, so the press is `Applied` lamp on or off, and the PC-7 (v) unlit re-check skips an `ACTOR_SELF` channel; the controller needs no change, only an acceptance criterion and the siblings' conformance *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, general rule G1)*.

- **AC-PCI-115** **GIVEN** the actor alone with the lamp on in a lit fixture and a damaged suit, **WHEN** `begin_patch` is submitted on `ACTOR_SELF`, **THEN** the result is `Applied` and `loco_state == CHANNELLING`; **GIVEN** the same state with the lamp **off** and no other light, **THEN** the result is `Applied` as well (option (a): `ACTOR_SELF` verbs are an `act_gate` exempt row, so the lit check is not applied) and the channel is not aborted `UNLIT` by the PC-7 (v) re-check. This is a conformance test against the siblings: it fails against the registry `act_gate` list, Interaction IA-6 and Emitter State EM-21 until they add the exemption (Open Question 16), and it is written so a stub that omits the exemption reproduces the old `NOT_LIT` answer. (auto with Interaction and Emitter stubs) [PC-6 lit-only rule; Open Question 16] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: new; blocking; re-review, general rule G1: lamp-off expected value is `Applied`)*
---
| 16 | **RESOLVED in this GDD (re-review 2026-10-27, general rule G1 with the re-review's recommendation) — option (a): `ACTOR_SELF` verbs are an `act_gate` exempt row; the siblings must conform before the vertical-slice story set.** The defect: the self-patch (`begin_patch` on `ACTOR_SELF`, Interaction IA-17 / IA-6, Emitter State EM-18 / EM-21, Suit SE-22), the only MVP suit repair, could never pass the lit check, because EM-21 adds the owner's own beam to the owner's `lux_pm` only ("not added to the owner's `act_lux_pm`"), the `lit` flag is computed from `act_lux_pm`, and Interaction lists `NOT_LIT` for `begin_patch`; the earlier closure citing EM-18 / EM-21 rested on a misreading (EM-18's exception covers the exposure sum, not the act gate) and stays withdrawn, and the foot origin sits 25–45 px below the chest point while the beam follows aim, not facing, so the "inside your own beam at every facing" condition could not hold either. The ruling: add `ACTOR_SELF` verbs to `act_gate`'s exempt rows beside `drop`, `toggle_beam`, the inspect card and `throw_glowstick` (registry `act_gate`, owner Interaction; smaller, keeps EM-21's rule intact for every other case); option (b) (amend EM-21) is not taken. Lamp on and lamp off both give `Applied`. **To conform (not edited here):** registry `act_gate` exempt list; Interaction IA-6 (and the IA-7 unlit re-check for `ACTOR_SELF` channels); Emitter State EM-21's note. The acceptance criterion is a conformance test (Interaction reach, focus & channels) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; re-review, general rule G1)* | Interaction; Emitter State | Next consistency pass — **blocks the MVP vertical slice until the siblings conform** |

**IA-6 Act only on what is lit (`act_gate`).** `act_gate(o) = in_reach(o) AND lit(o)`, where `in_reach` is the Controller's integer predicate (itself including the lit conjunct) and `lit` is Emitter State's hysteresis bit (`LIT_ON_PM`, `LIT_OFF_PM`, no dwell). Every PLAYER-origin Interaction command whose declaration is not exempt checks `act_gate` in `validate`, against the exposure table committed at tick T−1 (EM-25). The exceptions are exactly three, plus the actor verbs that are not object verbs: `drop` of the carried module, `toggle_beam`, and the inspect card of an already-lit instrument (PC-6); `throw_glowstick` is an actor verb like `toggle_beam` and needs no lit target (IA-29). **No fourth exception for the pod console (refused, stated here):** Web Map's ASK-I2 and Boarding's ASK-BS-I3 ask that `pod_hop` at the CONSOLE be exempt from the lit condition; the three exceptions are the Controller's PC-6 list (PCI:127) and IA-17 already refuses a fourth, so `pod_hop`, `berth` and `unberth` stay lit-gated, and the hop stays available by content, not by exemption: the docked pod's dock-room prop carries a small self-powered status glow that counts as an ordinary lit fixture (not a fourth `act_gate` exception), so `pod_hop`'s lit gate is always satisfied at the console and a `NOT_LIT` at a dock console is a content defect, not a state (Open Question 31, resolved) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: X2, Web Map option (B); this refusal STANDS. The self-powered fixture class (Emitter State EM-3 / EM-11), the placement rule and lint in every dock room (Derelict Authoring), the art-director's luminance separation from the visible-unknown lamp and Web Map accepting ASK-BS-W3 are the other owners' sides; Boarding's BS-19 invariant is owned jointly: Web Map and Emitter State guarantee the glow, Authoring lints its placement)*. An unregistered ref answers exactly as an unlit one (EM-21), so a phantom and a darkened real object are indistinguishable by design. *Why the rule exists:* it makes darkness a trade, not a free dodge of the web's attention — "unlit objects can be worked on" was rejected because working in the dark would be a free Attention dodge. Pillars: **P3** (every action spends exposure) and **P4** (reaching for a phantom finds nothing). *Decides:* PC-6, EM-21/22/25, F2 (the composite is registered as a formula, D.2).

**IA-17 Repair is real, incremental `repair_step`.** For `begin_patch` the hook, at every credited block (IA-14 row 8), calls `check_repair_step` and then M7 `repair_step(subject_kind, id, delta_bp, kind)` with `delta_bp` = `repair_step_delta` (D.1). `hp_at_begin` is read in the hook at the first step, never in `validate` (IA-11a). **Healthy-subject guard (Interaction's own, independent of the Graph's answer to the hp-clamp question):** the hook never calls M7 PATCH when `hp_at_begin ≥ LEAK_HP` **and** `cap_at_begin > PATCH_CAP_BP` (the subject has never been patched and nothing is leaking), and never calls M7 at all when `repair_step_delta ≤ 0`; such a job runs its full duration with zero mutator calls and resolves `PRECONDITION(NOTHING_TO_REPAIR)`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, BLOCKING, delegated G2 (the creative-director's Option B): the former threshold, `hp_at_begin` at or above the patch cap itself, left the silent band open: at true hp 4000 to 5999 a PATCH gained at most 1999 bp, permanently lowered `hp_cap` by 4000 bp and emitted the Graph's patch weep, which a healthy pipe does not, so a one-block tap-and-cancel probed a pipe's true state at the price of a block, the P4 failure Design Test 2 names. The guard is now keyed on the real harm: **both** `hp_at_begin` and `cap_at_begin` are read in the hook at the first step (the Graph's `node()` / `edge()` carry `hp_cap`, as M6's `SalvageRecord` does). A PATCH on a subject that is not leaking and has never been patched is "not a job a patch can do": silent damage is FULL work (Pillar 5), and the job runs the full bar and resolves `NOTHING_TO_REPAIR` identically at hp 10000, 5999, 5000 and 4000 with `hp_cap` 10000, with identical Graph state, descriptors and noise. 2. **Light is the price of agency.** *When a choice lets the player act without light vs. requires light to act → require light.* (the registry `act_gate` exemptions, four: `drop`, `toggle_beam`, the inspect card of an already-lit instrument and `throw_glowstick`; the first draft listed three) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* Otherwise working in the dark becomes a free Attention dodge and "go dark" degenerates into the dominant strategy.

**EM-21 — Subjects register; each has one anchor; an unregistered ref answers like an unlit one.** Anything that asks "am I lit" registers a **subject** with `register_subject(ref, kind, anchor_px, section_id)` (E6) and withdraws it with `unregister_subject(ref)` (E7). Subject kinds: OBJECT (an interaction anchor), ACTOR (the foot origin, *read* from `body.state` each tick, not supplied; its `section_id` and `body_id` are read the same way from Body's `actor_section(actor_id)` and `body_of_actor(actor_id)`, BDY-29, so the owner's exposure is attributed to the section the foot stands in and moves with it across a door), HORROR, ITEM (loose items). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The subject's single `anchor_px` is the only sampled point: a large object half in a beam is lit iff its anchor is (the same one-point model as `REACH_PX` and focus scoring, PC-6, and the cheapest symmetric one). Sections are never point-sampled; they aggregate by emitter list (`section_emission`, EM-27). `moving` is a per-registration flag: ACTOR and HORROR subjects are always moving; an ITEM registers static (a carried item is unregistered at pickup and re-registered at drop); only moving registrations count against `MAX_MOVING_SUBJECTS`. **The owner stands in their own light** *(orchestrator ruling: the systems-designer's SD-7 adopted with the checkpoint fix CP-9 — as first proposed it excluded the owner's beam from the owner's lux, so a player alone with the lamp on would have read `lux` 0 to Horror, the opposite of P3)*: the owner's own beam contributes its **full `output_pm`** — the d = 0 apex value, which EM-19 already places inside every cone — to the owner's ACTOR `lux_pm`, independent of facing and of occlusion, so the owner's self-lux never flips with the way they face; it is not added to the owner's `act_lux_pm` (the player is never the target of their own verb). Attention reads the beam as *emission* (`emitters()`, `section_emission`) and does not add the same beam again to the owner's lux (EM-27). Every other beam lights the owner, and the owner's beam lights everyone else, by the ordinary cone test. **An unregistered ref answers exactly like an unlit registered one** *(orchestrator ruling: SD-16 adopted — a P4 requirement)*: `lux(ref)` is 0 and `lit(ref)` is false in release builds, so the Perception Filter's phantom targets (kernel Open Question 14) cost Interaction the same check as real unlit ones and the query cannot become an existence oracle that undermines the phantom-loot hallucination. A debug-only `registered(ref)` exists for tests and the Debug Overlay. Registration over `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS` returns false, increments `emitter_subjects_overflow` and the subject reads dark (fails safe); a duplicate registration is a no-op returning false. **Runtime overflow is a content or budget defect, never a gameplay state** *(creative-director CD-GDD-ALIGN concern 3)*: failing safe to dark is the right behaviour for a subject the table cannot hold, but a real object sitting visibly inside a beam that refuses to prompt breaks design test 1 (the honest edge) and the P4 "reach for it" falsifier, because the player reads a real lit object as a hallucination. So the caps are held upstream by budgets, not discovered at run time (EM-24, D.15 I-CAPS (d)), and the two counters `emitter_subjects_overflow` and `emitter_moving_overflow` ship in release builds as telemetry (the probe counter went with the probes, EM-24) (a counter in the diagnostics block, not only a debug assertion), so a budget breach in a playtest or live build is visible and reportable. The subject table fields are below. Registrations are canonical (EM-28, R16): registrants (Interaction, Horror, Suit) own the thing registered and re-register idempotently in their own `post_restore`, which `restore_after` `emitter.state` allows.

**EM-18 — The illumination model: contribution, curve classes, saturating sum.** For one emitter and one subject, the contribution `c` is **0** unless all of: the subject's `body_id` equals the emitter's (EM-30), the subject is inside the emitter's radius (`d2 <= reach_px²`, a closed edge), inside its cone for cone shapes (EM-19), not blocked (EM-20). The one exception is the owner's own beam on the owner's ACTOR subject, which contributes its apex value, facing- and occlusion-independent (EM-21). For every other pair `c = ⌊output_pm * f(d, reach_px) / 1000⌋` (Formulas D.7), `d` the exact integer floor of the distance from the emitter's origin (the chest, for the beam). Two **curve classes** are carried as a data table so the Lighting spike can replace a curve without changing the API: **SOFT** (pools, fixtures, glowsticks, lanterns, fault glow) `f = 1000 * (R - d) / R`, linear to zero at the fade-out radius; **HARD** (the cones and the beacon) `f = EDGE_FLOOR_PM + (1000 - EDGE_FLOOR_PM) * (R - d) / R`, so the contribution at the rim of a full-output hard-edged emitter is `EDGE_FLOOR_PM` (placeholder 250 permille, range 160–400, owner technical-artist, confirmed by the Lighting spike) and the lit boundary **is** the drawn hard edge. *(orchestrator ruling: this is a deliberate deviation from the routed ruling's single default curve `c = output_pm * (R - d) / R`, which contradicts its own "hard outer edge exactly at `reach_px`" clause: with `LIT_ON_PM` 150 a full-output wide beam of reach 288 px would be actionable only to `d <= 244` px — 44 px, almost a full tile, inside the hard edge the player sees, the light visibly falling on a valve the hand cannot reach, which is the game lying (P1) and contradicts art bible hero #1. Three specialists converged on the edge-floor remedy; rejected: lowering `LIT_ON_PM` toward 0 (a near-black pixel becomes actionable — a different lie, and hysteresis dies) and redefining the "drawn edge" as an iso-line at 150 permille (contradicts the hard edge). Surfaced as a deviation from the ruling's default in the return value, not a registry conflict.)* The consequence is intended: a *dimmed* hard-edged emitter (output below `⌈LIT_ON_PM * 1000 / EDGE_FLOOR_PM⌉` = 600) has an honestly smaller actionable area; a full-output emitter is actionable to its last pixel (invariant I-EDGE: `BEAM_BASE_PM * EDGE_FLOOR_PM >= 1000 * LIT_ON_PM`). For SOFT classes the actionable radius `r_lit` is **the largest `d` whose integer chain (D.7) gives `c ≥ LIT_ON_PM`**, published by the sim per emitter as `r_lit_px` (the closed form ⌊R × (output_pm − LIT_ON_PM) / output_pm⌋ of the first draft ran 1 px high for some dimmed outputs and is not used) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, inside the fade-out radius `reach_px` by design (a full fixture of reach 144 px is actionable to 122 px); Lighting must draw a soft pool's readable boundary at the published `r_lit_px`, which the Lighting spike confirms (the art bible

| **DOWNED** | The Suit's `locomotion_cap` is NONE with `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS` running | Revive (Vertical Slice B), the solo "give up and reload" action (user ruling D7, the Controller's) or DEAD | Readings keep updating; the lamp stays lit; marks persist (FAILED / DOWNED persists the mark); no banner; walk-only is surfaced by the readings, never by text; the HUD draws nothing for the give-up action (any hint it needs is a plate request to the Controller and Interaction, not a HUD banner) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | Suit |

- **If the seat is DOWNED**: the readings keep updating, the lamp stays lit, the marks persist and pulse (or stay solid, HS-23), there is no banner and no tint, and the solo "give up and reload" action (user ruling D7) is the Controller's and draws nothing on the HUD; walk-only is surfaced by the breath and warmth readings *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. If the seat is restored into DEAD, no mark is drawn. (EC-HS-24)

**HS-53. Pause, DOWNED, DEAD, restore and transit.** *Rule.* The full state table is in States and Transitions. In brief: solo pause freezes the HUD undimmed, with one exception: an active mark is held ON solid (HS-23); DOWNED keeps the readings updating and the lamp lit with marks persisting; DEAD freezes the readings with no death screen, score or text; the first `RUNNING` frame after a restore draws the readings at restored values with no settle, no abort frame, no notch, clears every presentation-local counter (debounce, hold grid, bar fill, tick phases, flash history), and reads `restore_reason` only as a request, never altering hallucination content from `DEATH_STUB` (it keys only the one record line of HS-46); `TRANSIT_HOLD` and the pod leg leave the HUD's layout unchanged while statuses run in the pod (user ruling D60): the readings keep updating from `perceived` as in `RUNNING` and stay lie-capable, and a death in the pod is the Controller's `DEAD` (the DEAD state below). **Who owns the visible step from death to restore, and what it is** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; Save/Load SL-7)*: **Save/Load owns it, and it is automatic.** At the tick boundary where the seat becomes `DEAD`, Save/Load settles or abandons the in-flight write, picks a generation (SL-8) and calls `request_restore` with `restore_reason = DEATH_STUB`; the kernel enters `LOADING` (the command queue is flushed); the Pipeline shows layer-1 black (`TRANSIT_HOLD`) while the HUD stays unchanged, holding its last model; the first `RUNNING` frame is the `RESTORE_FRAME` below, with the camera cut at the pre-load zoom step. **The player presses nothing, and there is no designed dwell** (no death screen, no dim-out, no sound, SL-7), so the HUD's DEAD state lasts only until the restore completes; if no candidate loads (`SL_LOAD_NO_LOADABLE_SAVE`) the Chart Table shows a boot-flow screen (Save/Load OQ-42). The cryo re-wake sequence is Failure Contract & Re-wake's at Vertical Slice A. The HUD adds nothing to this step beyond the one record line on the first `RUNNING` frame (HS-46); AC-HS-132 and AC-HS-136 assert the HUD's side of it *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. **Whether the player understands why the game restarted** (P5 depends on it; the one peripheral line after a hard cut may read as a crash) is a **measured playtest question, OQ-HS-84** (pass bar: 7 of 8 testers can say why); the ruling is not re-opened, and any fix is owned by the world or by Save/Load, never by HUD text *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. *Why.* P5 and the user decision that MVP death restarts from the last autosave (owned by Save/Load).

**HS-42. Hold-to-confirm.** *Rule.* The same bar at SHORT on the focused control's plate, `CONFIRM_HOLD_S` 0.8 by default (48 ticks, 3 ticks per px; the player may adjust the hold, so the fill rate follows the Controller's `hold_pm` and the HUD holds no hold constant); release drains it (the Controller's own `b` drains at `CONFIRM_DRAIN_RATE`, D.10, and the HUD draws it); no Alarm Red, no mark, no dialog. **Two modes (`confirm_view.mode`, HS-6), both required at MVP:** `HOLD` fills the bar over `CONFIRM_HOLD_S`; `TAP` (the Controller's one-handed preset, `confirm_mode` `TAP`, `CONFIRM_TAP_WINDOW` 3 s) shows no fill but thickens the bracket and relabels the plate `verb_confirm_prompt` ("Confirm?") while the first tap is armed, and disarms on a focus or context change as the Controller says. **The locomotion class** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the table listed no `WALK → CARRY_WALK` on a pickup made while walking and no `CARRY_WALK → WALK / RUN` on drop, install or `clear_carry_ref`, yet Edge Cases and the AC use both, and only `IDLE / WALK → IN_POD` existed although `pod_hop` is also pressed while carrying or running; read literally the table either flagged every walking pickup as invalid or left `WALK` active with `carry_ref` set, applying the wrong stride, speed and noise class)*. `{IDLE, WALK, RUN, CARRY_WALK}` is **one class for transition legality**: every move between them is legal, and inside the class `loco_state` is a **pure function of `(octant, run, cap, carry_ref)` recomputed every tick by `controller.step`** — `IDLE` if `octant == NONE`; else `CARRY_WALK` if `carry_ref ≠ none`; else `RUN` if `run ∧ cap == FULL ∧ ¬stowed_heavy`; else `WALK` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: D18; `stowed_heavy` is a read view of Suit & Equipment / Item DB, an input of the same kind as `cap`, never a stat the Controller computes, so the pure function is now over `(octant, run, cap, stowed_heavy, carry_ref)`)*. No trigger is needed, so no mutator (`set_carry_ref`, `clear_carry_ref`, an install, a `pickup`, a `drop`) can leave the class inconsistent, and the diagnostics' "invalid pair" rule applies only to pairs with an endpoint outside the class. The class members may all enter `STAGGERED`, `DOWNED` and `IN_POD`. `CHANNELLING` is not a trigger-driven transition at all: it is **derived** from `channel_ref` by the precedence function in the step order below, so the legal same-frame release-W/press-E case (`set_move_intent {NONE}` applies, then `begin_*` validates against `intent_octant == NONE` and applies) yields `CHANNELLING` on that tick, and the per-tick class function can never overwrite it on the next. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the earlier "`IDLE` alone enters `CHANNELLING`" made that case an invalid pair, and the class function would have overwritten `CHANNELLING` on the next tick.)*

**`controller.step` order (normative).** One run per controlled actor per tick (divisor 1, `after: suit.vitals`, P3), in exactly this order *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: new; the sub-rules in PC-4, PC-7, PC-9, D.4, D.5, D.8 and D.14 are the detail of these steps)*:

1. **Cap edge.** Read `locomotion_cap` and compare it with the stored `cap_seen` (PC-9). A falling edge `FULL → WALK_ONLY` in any state except `DOWNED`, `DEAD` and `IN_POD` sets `stagger_end_tick := T + STAGGER_TICKS` (a stagger already running keeps its timer; a `SYSTEM` `stagger` command's `apply` has already set it in P2, with the same rule) and clears `channel_ref` and `channel_face`. Cap `NONE` outside `DEAD` sets, once, `T_downed := T` and `death_tick := T + DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS`, clears `channel_ref` and `channel_face`, and drops the carried module at the foot origin (kept while the body is the pod, D60). A cap rising from `NONE` clears `T_downed` and `death_tick`. Last, `cap_seen := cap`, in every state.
2. **Timers.** `stagger_end_tick ≤ T` clears it (the stagger ends on this tick). While `DOWNED`, `T ≥ death_tick` sets `loco_state := DEAD`; the cap was read first in step 1, so a recovery written on this tick wins (D.14), and a `give_up` apply has already lowered `death_tick` in P2.
3. **Movement wins over a channel.** `octant := intent_octant`. If `octant ≠ NONE` and `channel_ref` is set, clear `channel_ref` and `channel_face` **now**, so the move takes effect on this same tick and the first movement step is not lost.
4. **`loco_state`: one total precedence function**, highest first: `DEAD` (latches until a restore replaces the block) > `DOWNED` (`T_downed` set; also while the body is the pod, D60, so a downed actor in the pod is `DOWNED` and `give_up` is live) > `IN_POD` (the actor's `body_of_actor` is a pod body, a pure Body read) > `STAGGERED` (`stagger_end_tick` set) > `CHANNELLING` (`channel_ref` set) > the locomotion class function of `(octant, run, cap, stowed_heavy, carry_ref)`. **Every non-class exit lands directly on the class member (or the next flag down) on the tick its flag clears — a stagger ending, a `DOWNED` recovery, leaving the pod — with no intermediate `IDLE` tick** (the creative-director's lean: "escape is never blocked" serves Pillar 1, and a one-tick `IDLE` after a lock would be a tick of lost control; it also removes a state the class function would otherwise have to contradict).
5. **`v_eff`** from D.4 using the `loco_state` just computed (and the D.5 ladder when its knob is non-zero).
6. **Facing** from D.8, top-down, using the same `loco_state` and the stored `channel_face`.
7. **Bookkeeping and derived values:** `ramp_ticks`, `walk_ticks`, `last_octant`, `decel_k`, `chest_sim`, `hand_sim`; then the read view is published.

The precedence function's one deviation from the review's proposed order is `DOWNED` above `IN_POD`, forced by user ruling D60 (statuses run in the pod; a death there is the Controller's `DEAD`).

| Order | Test at elapsed `e` | If true |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `cancel_channel` | handled in P2, before the hook: the record is already gone and the hook does nothing |
| 1 | `channel_ref` absent (the Controller cleared it: stagger, downed, body transfer, restore) | `ABORT(BODY)`; no accrual |
| 2 | the target is no longer a registered subject (tombstoned) | `ABORT(TARGET_GONE)` |

| 6 | (`begin_harm`, and every ASSEMBLY-owned record) `e mod LIT_RECHECK_TICKS == 0` and the row's `eligible` predicate is false (the Sanity gate query; Assembly's `weld_offer` or `seam_cut_offer`, so a lost `docked` aborts the channel, MSA ASK I1 (viii)) | `ABORT(NOT_ELIGIBLE)` |
| 7 | none of the above and `e ≥ 1` | accrue tick `e`; push the verb's noise (IA-33) |
| 8 | `e mod B == 0` and `e ≥ B` | block `j = resume_blocks + e / B` is credited (`resume_blocks = resume_offset / B`, 0 for a fresh job). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: **every channel credits the block, then steps.** First, for every verb and both truth branches, set `blocks_done = j` (absolute) and `t_last_block = T`; then, for incremental channels only, run the **step**: `check_*` and the Class A mutator (`begin_patch`, FULL repair, the self-patch's `patch_integrity`), or `apply_suit_damage` for `begin_harm`.
